objective: Connect Treasurer to the canonical F06 render admission lifecycle while preserving Overseer command authority, Guardian capability authority, ComputeRouter physical placement, and F07 verification authority.

rulesConsidered: Overseer is the single sovereign command authority beneath Human Authority.
Treasurer owns economic admission but does not replace physical placement.
Workers do not own global economic resources.
F07 remains the independent verification boundary.

notes: F06 cannot use a Treasury-gated render without an Overseer command identity.
Production Treasury persistence remains fail-closed without a transaction-capable Mongo client.
F07 receipt identifiers are taken from F07ReleaseGuardian, not synthesized by Treasury or F06.
Production ComputeGateway is bound to the canonical Treasury service and validates the execution-scoped permit before physical dispatch.
Automatic provider failover is capped by the retry allowance carried in the Treasury permit.

conflicts.originalConflict: Connecting Treasurer to F06 could allow F06 to become its own settlement authority or cause ComputeRouter to inherit economic scheduling responsibilities.
conflicts.proposedResolution: Reserve in RenderFabric before ComputeRouter dispatch; return the reservation identity; settle only in F07 after an authentic F07ReleaseGuardian receipt; keep provider placement in ComputeRouter.
conflicts.acceptedResolution: F06 admits expenditure economically but cannot settle production spend or choose the physical provider.

conflicts.originalConflict: A provider can report COMPLETED without a physical output artifact; the economic hold must not remain indefinitely.
conflicts.proposedResolution: Release the Treasury reservation before propagating the artifactless completion failure.
conflicts.acceptedResolution: RenderFabric now releases the reservation on COMPLETED-without-artifact and fails the render.

conflicts.originalConflict: Legacy controller behavior allowed persistence fallback when MongoDB was unavailable, which could silently remove economic governance.
conflicts.proposedResolution: Require Treasury persistence in production and refuse boot when the transaction-capable MongoDB Treasury cannot initialize.
conflicts.acceptedResolution: FactoryOS now sets treasuryRequired by default in production and aborts boot when Treasury is unavailable.

conflicts.originalConflict: ComputeRouter automatic failover could cross provider boundaries without consuming a separately authorized retry envelope.
conflicts.proposedResolution: Carry maxRetries in the Treasury economic permit and cap physical provider attempts at 1 + maxRetries.
conflicts.acceptedResolution: Treasury zero-retry renders are limited to one physical provider attempt; additional retries require a new Overseer/Treasury reservation.

changes: Bound RenderIntent to overseerCommandId for Treasury-gated rendering.
Reserved an explicit Treasury economic envelope before F06 physical compute.
Released reservations on dispatch failure and F07 rejection.
Settled measured capacity only with an authentic signed F07ReleaseGuardian receipt.
Initialized a Mongo-backed Treasury service/account in the persistent controller.
Added focused render/Treasury admission tests and Wave 2 architecture records.
Closed an artifactless COMPLETED-receipt reservation leak in RenderFabric and added regression coverage.
Changed production boot to fail closed when Treasury cannot be initialized with transaction-capable MongoDB.
Bound the production ComputeGateway to the Treasury service so render dispatch cannot bypass the economic authority.
Extended economic permits with execution scope and retry allowance; ComputeGateway revalidates the permit before dispatch.
Capped automatic compute failover attempts by the Treasury-authorized retry envelope.
Added regression coverage for permit propagation and scope replay rejection.
